_comment: Guided tour of Plugin Check. Every step points at a real control; the two that need the user's hands wait for them (picking a row, starting a safe sweep). 'name' is the emtk control: the table, a button's action or a field's attr.

steps.title: What a check proves
steps.text: Plugin Check builds the native window of each plugin in a separate process and draws it once. A pass means the window opens without an error; it does not mean the science is right. Nothing here touches your own settings: every check runs on throw-away ones.

steps.title: One row per plugin
steps.text: The table lists every plugin ChiSurf discovered, built-in and your own. Click a header to sort, type in the filter box to narrow it, and right-click the header to choose columns. pending rows (not yet checked) are dimmed until a sweep has reached them.

steps.title: Pick a plugin
steps.text: Select any row. The window on the right fills in with its module, source, dependencies and description, and, once it has been checked, the whole error.

await.hint: Click any row in the table.

steps.title: The details
steps.text: Requires must load before the plugin; Optional ones are reached later. Problems appears when the dependency resolver finds a requirement that is missing or out of range.

steps.title: How a sweep behaves
steps.text: Delay between plugins pauses between two checks. Skip blacklisted leaves out plugins that failed five times in a row, so a broken one does not slow every sweep.

steps.title: Run a safe sweep
steps.text: Test safe plugins checks only the first ten plugins with a short timeout, a quick way to see how a sweep looks. Test all plugins checks everything and takes minutes.

steps.title: Watch it run
steps.text: The bar and the status line count the plugins; the Status column fills in as each result arrives. Stop ends the sweep and terminates the plugin being checked.

steps.title: Start over
steps.text: Refresh rescans the plugin folders and clears the results; Clear blacklist lets blacklisted plugins be checked again.
